description: Use native-procedure-references to page retained procedure reference or unresolved-call rows. Endpoint kind selected-procedure refers to the summary procedure, null preserves the original null, and shared carries an index into items.endpoints, where each other procedure is stored once per page. Exact source_address and target_address filters apply to reference rows. For inspect_api_contract parents, graphql-contract pages retained SDL types/fields, operation definitions, field references, fragment-spreads or diagnostics with exact filters and selected columns. Use javascript-routes collections to query route patterns, source-linked occurrences, source status, unknowns or summary counts from retained JavaScript application or web-bundle Evidence. Use web-bundle collections endpoints or inferences to page endpoint observations and inferences from retained analyze_web_bundle Evidence; summary returns target URL, origin, and counts. For retained trace_feature Evidence, kind native-feature-trace pages matches, references or unknowns; matches filter exact address, references filter exact source_address and target_address, source_index identifies each original row, and list_unknowns pages durable question heads. Inspect selected views of supported completed Evidence without repeating analysis. Use recorded-array with an exact raw_result object-member path to page a provider-recorded array when the producer supplies that path; rows keep their raw meaning and the parent retains coverage. For procedure_pseudo_code Evidence, summary reports text availability and the original selection; kind native with facet pseudocode pages the original UTF-16 text. Other native facets require analyze_function. Choose a view compatible with the parent operation described below. Command summary views preserve ordered GDB records or opaque objdump stdout/stderr once, source parameters, completion facts and parent identity. They do not establish current target state. Historical capture summaries return identity and counts without bodies or archive inventories. Capture views page retained records: view {kind: "capture", detail: "preview" | "complete", offset: 0, limit: 20}; preview selects recorded headline fields and binary descriptors, complete returns exact records with all sidecars. Offsets follow the selected parent record order, preserving original producer ordinals. Paging never reopens the source or reruns the decoder. Native export tables use kind native-exports, collection exports/issues, exact names or original indices, selected fields and matching-row pagination; parent Evidence plus source_index identifies each row. Source coverage stays separate from page coverage. BEAM views use kind beam, collections atoms/exports/imports/lambdas/chunks, exact names/indices/fields and matching-row pages; import modules intersects function names. source_index identifies original parent-and-collection rows, preserving every arity and raw atom index. beam.counts preserves null missing tables versus decoded empty tables; runtime absence remains unknown. PYC views use kind python-pyc, collection code_objects, names/indices/fields and paging; source_index scopes every same-name alternative to the parent, nested_code keeps code-constant references, and pyc.coverage preserves source coverage. Go metadata uses kind go, collection dependencies/settings, exact paths/keys or indices, fields and pagination. Row index refers to the original collection; empty selections return no rows, and dependency coverage remains unknown. Rust metadata uses kind rust, collection packages/edges, exact names/versions or original indices, selected fields, edge from_indices/to_indices and matching-row pagination. Embedded-record coverage is separate from unknown runtime dependencies. For inspect_pcap_capture parents, kind pcap pages endpoints, dns-queries, tls-sni, protocols, http-uris or unattributed-addresses. Select an exact query for dns-addresses, or a tshark/capinfos stream for UTF-16 diagnostics text. Page totals count retained facts; source coverage remains explicit. Qlog summaries keep profile/scope and counts; kind qlog pages traces, streams, loss-declarations, incomplete-records, contributions, ranges or final-sizes. Except traces, select trace_index; stream-specific facets also require exact stream_id and direction. Facts retain all-recorded-events-before-selection scope, and interval overlap or endpoint loss declarations do not prove retransmission or network loss. The api-surface view groups retained HAR requests by method, origin and format-rule path template; templated segments are inferences. It reads no headers or bodies and reports no query values. The environment-manifest view projects the same HAR requests on the primary origin (most JSON-like records) into a replayable tool surface: view {kind: "environment-manifest", template_rules: ["after-uid-literal", "opaque-token", "sibling-variance"], include_query_parameter_names: true}. Each tool has a deterministic name, a path template and parameters from the four format rules plus the selected opt-in rules, observed query parameter names, a value-free body shape for POST/PUT/PATCH, status and content-type sets and record ordinals; records are pointers into the parent, excluded groups carry a reason and three fixed unknowns are always stated. Templates, parameters and names are inferences; the view copies no header, cookie or body values and refuses parents inspected with sensitive values. A capture_browser_scenario parent also supports summary and browser-scenario steps/events/transactions/text pages, preserving step_indices, event_kinds, transaction_ids and selected artifacts. A capture_browser_scenario parent that selected response bodies or header values projects the same way, one record per network transaction in request order; it relies on capture-time redaction of declared secrets instead of that refusal, and a transaction whose URL was redacted is left unrepresented. The environment-state view extracts, from the same parents, the initial state the recorded reads observed: view {kind: "environment-state", template_rules: [...]} with the rules of the manifest it accompanies. It reads response bodies recorded before the first related write and reports entity types with an identity field (proved by a path parameter or inferred from a field name), entities in collection order with per-view values where views differ, documents for non-parameterized reads that are not entities and have one initial request line (item-shaped paths stay recorded), and a render plan per read tool: item and list views reproduce their latest recordings from the state (a list also learns the filters, search, sort and paging its recordings verify, and answers new values of them from the state), and every other read tool is a recorded view with a reason. It also reports a write plan per state-changing tool (create, update, delete or document, built from its first successful call) and write_clock; a plan is served only when replaying the capture shows a later read confirming its effect and none contradicting it. Types and identity are inferences; values are recorded data, so it refuses parents inspected with sensitive values, and a scenario parent must have selected response bodies; its values keep the capture redaction markers, and a write whose URL it redacted ends the state of every type. The environment-coverage view, view {kind: "environment-coverage", template_rules: [...]}, summarizes that state without its entities: reads.state and reads.recorded count read tools answered from the state and replayed (recorded_reasons per view reason), writes.served lists the served write tools, and writes.withheld lists each other write tool with its reason, plan record, contradicting read and a hint about what to record next; it refuses what the environment-state view refuses. For a retained record use source: {kind: "retained-evidence", evidence_id: "<parent_evidence_id>"}. Use normalized_result.parent_evidence_id from a summary receipt. Source kind is required. Portable source uses {kind: "inline", evidence: <complete Evidence>}. A completed Evidence JSON file on this host uses {kind: "evidence-file", path: "<absolute path>"}: REA reads and authenticates it, then projects it like retained Evidence, so a large capture is bounded by the file reader rather than by inline-input accounting. The file may also be an Evidence bundle written by CLI --evidence_output or export_evidence_bundle; select evidence_id when it contains more than one record. For layout, JavaScript, inventory, WASM, Mach-O, Interface Builder, EVM, managed artifact, Android package and Dart AOT sources, request a summary with view: {kind: "summary"}; summary is a view kind and has no facet. The WASM summary gives validation, counts, WAT digest/length, tool profile and execution/network states without reading WAT text. Select a layout mitigations/linkage facet, one section/symbol/module, or a stable page. Module pages include assets, bundled and source modules; use node_id for ambiguous or unavailable paths. Typed module references use view {kind: "javascript", collection: "modules", projection: "references", where: {path: "main.js", kind: "javascript-module"}, offset: 0, limit: 64}; where matches exact retained strings (null selects unavailable paths). Rows include canonical identity, retained source-range count and observation support states. Source coverage and selection remain explicit; exhausting matching rows does not prove runtime loading or complete analysis. For exact file/native facts and processing gaps, use view {kind: "javascript-facts", where: {paths: ["package.json"]}, property_keys: ["name", "operation", "analysis_status"]}. Rows page original observations with canonical identities and Evidence; missing properties remain omitted. Paths match recorded artifact-path/source-range locations; optional kinds filter nodes. To discover field names without values, opt into include_available_property_keys: true with property_keys: []. Canonical identity and Evidence are separate from properties; keep each node_id/observation_id pair together when composing results. Inventory uses view: {kind: "inventory", collection: "occurrences", logical_paths: ["package.json"], offset: 0, limit: 64}. Inventory views page nodes, occurrences, edges or integrity contradictions. Occurrences accept exact logical_paths and occurrence_ids; nodes accept artifact_ids. Batch filters intersect (omitted means all available, [] means none); fields selects columns while retaining identity links. source_complete describes retained graph membership; source_coverage describes producer coverage, including unknown encrypted PCK directories. Page exhaustion does not prove absence in a partial source. WASM views use kind wasm and facet sections/imports/exports/candidates/glue/wat/headers/details/tool_profile; text facets use UTF-16 code units and source forms remain exact. Mach-O views use kind macho and facet entrypoints/architectures/build_metadata/load_commands/dependencies/imports/exports/segments/provenance; source_exhaustive false means unreturned rows may exist. Interface Builder views use kind interface-builder and collection documents/nodes/edges/coverage; nodes and edges accept an exact document relative_path. EVM summary returns all inferred interface candidates, carrier/decoded identities and explicit unknowns without hex or duplicate stdout. EVM views use kind evm and facet functions/bytecode_hex/stdout/stderr; function pages preserve the original candidate rows, and text offsets/limits count UTF-16 code units (hex has two characters per decoded byte). Exhausting candidate pages does not establish global interface completeness. Managed artifact summaries preserve complete identity/classification, metadata status, module/MVID, frameworks, coverage and limitations without unrelated inventories. Managed pages use kind managed and collection references/resources/attributes, retaining source coverage and build-local token scope; page exhaustion does not establish complete metadata. Managed member summaries keep identity, selection with unmatched names, coverage and per-collection counts; managed-members pages use collection types/exported_types/fields/methods/member_refs/call_edges/field_accesses/user_strings. Exact names and declaring_types filters intersect before paging where supported; fields selects columns (distinct from collection: "fields"). Identity/source_index, module MVID, source coverage and unresolved filter counts remain; omit body to avoid IL anchors. Omitted fields preserves full rows. Android package summaries retain all declarations, engine identity and counts without decoded manifest text. Android manifest pages use kind android, facet manifest, offset and limit in UTF-16 code units; source_status preserves partial decoded coverage even when the retained text page is exhausted. Dart AOT summary preserves target/ABI/library identity, snapshot headers and pool lower bounds. String pages use kind dart-aot, collection package_uris/dart_uris/class_like_tokens; source coverage remains partial when the producer says partial. Protobuf views use kind protobuf, collection bodies/frames/fields, with record_ordinals, body_pointers and fields; field pages also select frame_indices, field_ids, field_numbers or schema_names. Byte identity, offset basis and body status remain present. Text and schema_value are opt-in page columns. APK signing views use kind apk-signature and collection signers/digests/lineage, with ids, signer_ids, schemes, fields and paging. Identity links remain when fields is empty. Declared identities and digest matches do not establish signature verification or authenticity. Model views use kind model-artifact and collection metadata (keys), tensors (names/types) or types (derived totals), with indices, fields and paging. Header SHA-256 scopes declarations; full-file identity remains unknown unless full hashing was selected. Arrays retain typed eight-element previews with explicit omissions. IL2CPP metadata views use kind il2cpp-metadata and collection sections/images/types/methods/fields/properties/events/parameters/string_literals/code_gen_modules/method_addresses/return_types/field_types/parameter_types/generic_method_instances/generic_method_issues. Select indices, fields and pages; sections/images/types/methods/fields/properties/events/parameters/return_types/field_types/parameter_types/generic_method_instances accept exact names (native type names match retained rendered values, preserving same-name rows; null names never match), types also accept image_indices/namespaces/declaring_types, and methods/members accept declaring_types. Parameters and parameter_types accept method_indices; code_gen_modules accept image_indices; method_addresses and generic_method_instances accept addresses/states (generic_method_instances also method_indices), preserving every folded alternative; generic_method_issues accept rows. Row index is scoped to the metadata digest; native pages add binary_source. Uncollected native tables have null counts and remain unavailable. Desktop directory views use kind desktop-application and collection files/omissions/candidates/components/next_probes, with fields and pagination; files and omissions accept exact paths or their stable IDs, and candidates accept families. Source coverage and stable row IDs remain available. Native load-image Evidence uses kind native-load-image with collection source_files/mappings/relocations/entry_points/entry_context/checks/sections, original indices, collection-specific fields and offset/limit paging. Null collections remain unrecorded or inapplicable; pages preserve unsupported verification. Native inventory Evidence from list_names, list/search_procedures or list/search_strings uses view: {kind: "native-inventory", offset: 0, limit: 64, fields: ["value"]}. Rows keep source_index and address even with selected fields. Summary counts describe retained rows; provider discovery coverage remains unknown. Native function Evidence accepts kind summary for identity, availability and facet counts, or kind native for selected facts: view: {kind: "native", facet: "procedure"}. Facets select procedure, pseudocode, assembly, basic blocks, comments, callers/callees, references, unresolved calls, referenced strings/names, native_api and value-flow observations. For parameter type paths when value flow is recorded, use facet: "value_flow_parameters"; its decompiler-observed path may be passed to inspect_native_data_type, but exact database lookup can be unavailable and does not by itself establish type identity. Use nonnegative offset and a positive caller-selected limit (defaults 0 and 64); pseudocode uses UTF-16 code units, other native pages use rows. Retained batch_decompile Evidence accepts kind summary for counts and sizes, or view: {kind: "batch-decompile", collection: "items", where: {statuses: ["unavailable", "error"]}} for body-free rows with exact indices, addresses, procedure_addresses or statuses (include_pseudocode adds bodies), or collection "pseudocode" with an index to page one body. Returns artifact identity, parent Evidence ID, a distinct view digest, coverage, limitations and unknowns. Actual serialized size determines MCP transport admission; choose a smaller page or export the complete retained Evidence if needed.

inputSchema.description: Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.

name: inspect_analysis_view

__schema119.description: One-based lines, zero-based UTF-16 columns; start inclusive, end exclusive.

__schema12.description: Verbatim direct-request path; not part of semantic identity.

__schema13.description: Verbatim auxiliary input paths keyed by argument name; caller assertions outside semantic identity.

source_parameters.description: Null means source parameters were omitted to fit the page; retrieve the parent Evidence.

path.description: Exact object-member path from the parent Evidence raw_result to the recorded array. The provider defines the values and their coverage.
Original ZIP member name reported by the reader

paths.description: Exact original ZIP member names; logical_path is separate

status.description: decoded is an instruction at the address; not-instruction-boundary is inside a listed instruction; data is defined data; outside-memory is outside the program's memory. Ghidra's not-in-listing means the address is in memory with no listed instruction or defined data; no decode was attempted, and memory may be uninitialized. The legacy undecodable value in older Evidence has the same ambiguous meaning and does not prove decoding failed.

primary.description: Provider primary-reference status, not proof of literal addressing or a runtime access. Null or omission means unavailable.

provenance.description: Provider subsystem reporting this reference; null or omission means unavailable.

source.description: Provider reference origin, such as analysis, default, imported or user_defined; null or omission means unavailable.

path_prefix.description: Exact string prefix; no URL/path normalization.

node_ids.description: Select terminal paths that visit any of these exact node identities. Omitted selects all; [] selects none.

seed.description: Whether this node matched the trace seed (a trace root).

include_observations.description: Opt into each selected node's complete retained observations, including properties and provenance.

node_ids.description: Select edges whose source or target is one of these exact node identities. Omitted selects all; [] selects none.

include_pseudocode.description: Opt into each selected successful item's complete pseudocode. Otherwise rows report pseudocode_code_units only.

addresses.description: Exact caller-selected symbols or addresses as submitted. Omitted selects all; [] selects none.

indices.description: Exact zero-based positions in the original batch, which keep duplicate selectors distinct. Omitted selects all; [] selects none.

procedure_addresses.description: Exact observed canonical entries. An item with unknown procedure identity never matches. Omitted selects all; [] selects none.

statuses.description: Item outcomes. Omitted selects all; [] selects none.

index.description: Exact item position from a row.

limit.description: UTF-16 code units in this page. A page size only: coverage reports the complete body and the next offset.

offset.description: UTF-16 code-unit offset into this item's text.

templated_groups.description: Groups across every page that carry at least one templated segment.

include_query_parameter_names.description: Include distinct observed query parameter names and their original record ordinals; names do not establish required parameters or a complete API schema.

name.description: Kebab-case environment name derived from the primary origin host.

origin.description: Primary origin: the origin with the most JSON-like records.

records.description: Pointers to the retained parent records cited by tools; no bodies.

templated_groups.description: Tools and excluded groups that carry at least one templated segment.

api_surface_template.description: Four-rule template of the tool's earliest record.

include_query_parameter_names.description: Include distinct observed query parameter names per tool; names do not establish required parameters or a complete API schema.

template_rules.description: Opt-in template rules applied after the four format rules, each listed at most once: after-uid-literal templates the segment following a literal uid, opaque-token templates long mixed alphanumeric segments, sibling-variance merges groups that differ in one identifier-like segment, sibling-pair-variance merges groups that differ in two adjacent literals between a plural literal and another literal when at least three distinct pairs vary in both, prefix-variance templates a literal at a position another tool templates by one of the other opt-in rules after the same preceding segments, at any method or length, when the literal is one of that parameter's observed values, carries a digit and has the length and character classes of one, or has the single length (eight or more characters) every observed value has and only their character classes. Literal sibling folding into existing opt-in parameters also requires sibling-variance. Merged parameters are inferences.

entities.description: Entities in collection order: type, collection, then first sighting.

timeline.description: Records are ordered by recorded start time, or by record order when any start time is missing.

id_basis.description: path-parameter: item responses repeat the requested path value in this field; field-name: inferred from listed items as the first identity name, else the first field ending in Id or _id shown distinct across at least two items, that every listed item carries distinctly.

init_before_ordinal.description: First recorded write whose path root relates to the type; state comes from records that finished before it.

volatile_fields.description: Fields whose recorded values changed with no recorded write between; the state keeps the latest.

template_rules.description: Opt-in template rules as for environment-manifest, each listed at most once. Use the rules of the manifest the state accompanies so tool names match.

deleted_flag.description: Member its reads set true on an entity the application soft-deleted.

envelope_ordinal.description: Record whose response, with the entity object replaced, every item response shares.

all_record_ordinals.description: With recorded membership, the checked lines that each listed every entity of their collection in state order, with only paging parameters starting at zero; a call answered on one lists the whole collection. Absent when none does.

counters.description: Envelope members that count the listed entities: a top-level member's name, or a JSON pointer to one in a top-level object beside the list (`/pageInfo/totalRows`); a top-level name starting with `/` is written as its pointer (`/~1total`).

listed_ids.description: Top-level envelope members listing each listed entity's identity field in list order, as Paperless's `all` does.

membership.description: all: every entity of the collection in state order; recorded: the entities each recorded response listed, except on the lines all_record_ordinals names.

query.description: How the view's other checked lines select and order entities, when filters, a search, a sort or paging explain them; absent when none does.

write_clock.description: The instant a served clock starts from: the end of the capture's last timed record.

writes.description: One plan per tool whose method may change state: its modelled effect, and whether the capture's later reads confirmed it (served).

recorded.description: Read tools that replay their recordings.

recorded_reasons.description: Replayed read tools per reason, as the environment-state view names the reasons.

state.description: Read tools answered from the state.

template_rules.description: Opt-in template rules as for environment-manifest, each listed at most once. Use the rules of the manifest the environment serves so tool names match.

contradicted_by.description: The read that disagreed with the modelled effect.

exemplar_ordinal.description: The first successful recorded call the plan was built from.

hint.description: What to record next; advice that never changes what is served.

page_truncated.description: This page omits retained nodes, and the edges they source, before offset or after next_offset.

traversal.description: complete: no trace budget, fixed node-payload allowance, provider p-code limit, ambiguous-candidate policy or unconfirmed provider cleanup stopped or narrowed the traversal; failed analyses and unresolved calls remain in unknowns. truncated: reasons lists each observed cause in schema order.

mi.description: The console command's independently framed MI result record; empty when a separate read-only query proves completion but raw stdout prevents identifying the original result class.

preview_truncated.description: More retained files have probe issues than fit in the preview.

container_file_offset.description: Offset of the selected slice from the start of the input Mach-O container; null when unknown.

name.description: Exact architecture name selected from lipo output; null when selection is unknown.

path.description: Selected artifact path; empty when explicitly excluded from Evidence.

sha256.description: Observed SHA-256; null only when explicitly excluded.

limitation_count.description: Number of parent Evidence limitations returned with this summary, including inherited provenance caveats.

before_url.description: Present only when it differs from the previous step's after_url (always for step 0).

limitations: This Evidence predates the manifest component projection; run inspect_android_package again to obtain it.

facet_availability.description: The provider's declared availability per facet, or null when it declared none. Unavailable facets name their reason here and in unknowns.

available.description: Provider facet_availability for pseudocode when declared; otherwise whether decompiled text is present. The flag is authoritative over raw length.

code_units.description: Pseudocode length in UTF-16 code units, the unit inspect_analysis_view pages pseudocode by.

truncated.description: True only when value-flow is available and the provider truncated it; false when value-flow is unavailable (see available).

semantic_discovery.description: On an unmatched string seed, retained semantic labels and direct string call arguments use the requested match mode and case sensitivity. Use a trace_seed with trace_javascript_semantics; source coverage limits absence claims.

label_unavailable.description: Resolved items whose entry label is null, whether the provider had none or its lookup failed.

path.description: Exact node path; required for properties and optional for nodes

names.description: Exact PE names, or UTF-8 ELF source names. ELF display fallbacks and names with unknown encoding are not identities; use indices for those rows. Omitted includes all names; [] matches none.

fields.description: Select record fields; address and source_index preserve identity. Selecting value also retains its string and decoding qualifications. Omit for every recorded field. Search tools filter before retention.

address.description: Select rows with this exact retained address.

source_classifications.description: Provider-reported source classifications; omission means none were supplied. The list need not exhaust all kinds.

source_address.description: Select this exact retained source address.

target_address.description: Select this exact retained target address.

source_address.description: Match an exact retained source address.

target_address.description: Match an exact retained target address.

fields.description: Omit to return every recorded field in each selected row.
Omit to return every recorded field in each selected row.
Defaults to address, segment, offset, status, type, symbol and values. Select original_bytes_hex or memory_bytes_hex explicitly.
Omit to return every recorded field in each selected row.

Omit to return every recorded field in each selected row.

protobuf.description: Flat decoding facts for explicitly selected records. Field indices are local to a body; offset_basis states whether ranges refer to retained or base64-decoded bytes. Interpretations without a caller-supplied schema are candidates.

artifacts.description: Return only selected artifact payloads; omitted_artifacts names the other recorded sections.

event_kinds.description: Omitted selects all event kinds; [] selects none.
Metadata events by default; select network-content explicitly for bodies and header values. [] returns identity and source indices only.

limit.description: Caller-selected UTF-16 code units, matching offset.

query_index.description: Zero-based index in the full retained dns_queries array, independent of page offset; use it to select one occurrence when display and wire identity remain ambiguous.

query_labels_hex.description: Select the exact retained wire label bytes for this query display. Null selects unknown identity, including historical records with the field omitted; omit this selector to match any identity.

fields.description: Original index always retained. Default attributes omit dependency vectors; select dependencies explicitly for direct index references.

path.description: Exact observed module path or original source-map reference from a module page; an empty reference is valid.

name.description: Exact UTF-8 section or symbol name, matched against retained source bytes. Use index for non-UTF-8 names or unresolved name bytes.

include_available_property_keys.description: Opt into original property names for each returned observation, without unselected values. Use with property_keys: [] to discover fields before reading them.

property_keys.description: Exact retained observation-property names to read; [] requests identities/provenance only. Missing properties remain omitted, distinct from retained null. No cross-observation merging or inferred values.

paths.description: Exact Evidence artifact-path or source-range source strings. Omitted includes unknown locations; [] matches none. No filesystem lookup or path normalization.

file_offset.description: LC_MAIN entry offset from the start of the selected Mach-O slice.
Offset from the start of the input Mach-O container.

path_bytes_hex.description: Original load-command path bytes before the first NUL; omitted in older Evidence.

file_offset.description: Offset from the start of the selected Mach-O slice.

file_offset_hex.description: Exact slice-relative file offset when it cannot be represented as a safe JSON integer.

file_size_hex.description: Exact file size when it cannot be represented as a safe JSON integer.

name_bytes_hex.description: Original segment-name bytes before the first NUL; omitted in older Evidence.

alignment_exponent.description: Exact binary alignment exponent when the corresponding byte alignment is not a safe JSON integer.

file_offset.description: Offset from the start of the selected Mach-O slice.

name_bytes_hex.description: Original section-name bytes before the first NUL; omitted in older Evidence.

segment_bytes_hex.description: Original segment-name bytes before the first NUL; omitted in older Evidence.

size_hex.description: Exact section size when it cannot be represented as a safe JSON integer.

vm_size_hex.description: Exact VM size when it cannot be represented as a safe JSON integer.

architecture.description: lipo slice name matched by CPU type, subtype and offset; null when unmatched.

commands.description: Encryption load commands in table order; a slice with more than two keeps the first two and states the count in reason.

container_end.description: Exclusive end offset from the start of the input file.

content.description: ciphertext when cryptid is nonzero; analysis derived from those bytes does not describe program code.

segment.description: File-backed segment holding these bytes; null when unmapped.

vm_start.description: VM address of slice_start; null when unmapped or when the segment has no VM size.

sections.description: File-backed sections the range overlaps; zero-fill and empty sections are excluded.

slice_end.description: Exclusive end offset from the start of the slice.

status.description: absent only when every load command was read; malformed and unknown carry a reason.

document.description: Exact documents[].relative_path; selects rows whose evidence names that archive.

constant.description: Field-owned ECMA-335 Constant declaration and decoded default. Null means neither a declaration nor HasDefault was observed; omission means historical Evidence without this inspection.

class_token.description: Raw build-local catch type token; not a cross-artifact identity

class_type_identity_resolved.description: Whether this artifact's local token identifies the reported catch type; null when unexamined

class_type_name_sha256.description: Nested nominal TypeDef/TypeRef name digest; assembly scope is compared separately and local tokens are not cross-artifact identities

il_sha256.description: SHA-256 of exactly the raw il_size CIL bytes; excludes the method header, locals signature, alignment, and extra sections

local_var_signature.description: Validated LocalVarSig blob facts; null when absent or unrecorded. Named types, modifiers and generic variables require metadata or declaring context; equal raw digests do not establish their cross-artifact type identity.

normalized_il_sha256.description: Member-result-v1 SHA-256 of UTF-8 JSON [opcode, operand_kind, operand] tuples for a complete decode; retains build-local tokens, omits switch targets, and excludes headers, locals, and exception regions

target_name.description: Method name; a method-spec target reports its generic method

value.description: Decoded UTF-16 code units, excluding the terminal flag byte; unpaired surrogates are kept

note_coverage.description: Complete only after all declared ELF note sections were examined within supported AMD metadata coverage; partial retains only examined facts.

shared_bytes.description: PTX: entry-local declared static bytes; CUDA ELF: allocated section bytes; AMDGPU: group_segment_fixed_size. Runtime dynamic/module shared allocations are not established by PTX.

declaring_type.description: Enclosing TypeDefinitionIndex derived from nestedTypes; -1 means no enclosing metadata type was recorded
Declared TypeDefinitionIndex from this MethodDefinition; -1 is an absent reference

path.description: Selected artifact path, or the canonical resource root when resource-only Evidence has no executable subject.

__schema227.description: The traced subgraph's coverage, or null when no seed matched.

__schema237.description: Exact trace node identities. Omitted selects all; [] selects none.

__schema274.description: Provider committed by the batch's upstream analysis profile, or null when the parent records none.

name.description: Provider's entry label, or null when unavailable.

__schema287.description: Caveats of this item's own provider observation when it supplied no pseudocode, including any reason the provider reported.

__schema324.description: Primary origin, as the environment manifest selects it.

__schema331.description: JSON pointer to the entity object or array within the response: the root or one member, or for an item the element of a one-element array there (/0 or /<member>/0).

__schema332.description: Ordered fields the view shows of each entity.

__schema335.description: Latest init record per request line that the view reproduced from the state.

__schema337.description: Top-level members minted per response, such as a request id: a UUID or clock that differed on every repeat of every concrete path the view answers with no write between. Checks leave them out; serving keeps the recorded value, so a served response repeats it.

__schema339.description: How the view spells clock fields it always spells otherwise than the entities' stored values; a stored value the view never recorded is spelled this way.

__schema342.description: The keys the view shows of object fields it always shows with fewer keys than an entity stores, such as a parent listed without its own nested type; a stored object the view never recorded shows those keys.

__schema344.description: Fields whose string arrays the view lists in code-point order, whatever order they were written in; learned from a read that shows a written array sorted.

__schema347.description: Recorded reads left to replay: they asked for some fields only (`fields`, `select`), or show the entities in another representation than the checked lines (an augmenting or reducing query). Replayed calls do not show served writes.

__schema349.description: Query keys that pick calls of the replayed reads out: a parameter only they name, a value only they give a parameter, or (absent) a parameter every checked line names and they leave out. A call matching any key replays; a projection parameter's value is tested on its own: a call replays unless every value it gives is `*` or one a checked line gave, and no replayed read gave it.

parameters.description: What each query parameter does. A call whose every parameter has a role is answered by evaluating them over the state.

record_ordinals.description: Checked lines the query reproduces, answered by evaluating it.

totals.description: Observed envelope members with reproducible counts of every match before paging, named as counters are; absent or unknown representations stay recorded.

field.description: Entities whose field equals the value as text, or whose array field holds it directly or as an object's id, slug or name.

fields.description: Entities with a string field containing a plain substring value, ignoring case using Unicode simple case folding; an empty value matches every entity. Syntax-like operators replay instead.

oneOf.description: Orders by the field the value names (`name`, `-name`, `name:desc`, `name-ASC`): numbers by value, text ignoring case, null last ascending.
asc or desc for the sort parameter.
Page size; zero or a negative value lists every match.

first.description: The first page, 0 or 1, when recordings distinguish the convention.

values.description: Recorded values that change nothing the view lists; other values are not computed.

address.description: How a call names its entities when its path does not end in one: the action segment after the item's id, or the body's ids as an array of one JSON `kind` or as objects carrying the id field, at the root or under `member`.

body.description: Body members the application stored as sent (accepted), members accepted only with their recorded value (fixed), members every call sends (required), the JSON type a later call stored an accepted member as when the observation does not show it (kinds), the member a call wraps its object in as a one-element array (envelope), the value a create stores for an accepted member a call leaves out, as a call that left it out showed (defaults), and members a recorded create sent empty, which a call that leaves them out is applied as sending (blank).

checked_record_ordinals.description: Later reads that reproduced from the state after this write.

collection.description: For a create whose recorded values are tied to its collection, the only collection it writes to.

exemplar_ordinal.description: The first successful recorded call the plan was built from.

observation.description: The record whose response showed the written entity or document, and a JSON pointer to it.

rules.description: How written fields get their values; unlisted fields of a created entity keep the observed value.

target.description: The entity type an entity effect writes, or the document view a document write changes.

read.description: A write's later read of the entity: an item read lends a create fields the response lacks, and its clock spellings; a list read only adds fields the response lacks.

unloaded.description: JSON pointers into the entity to values the response had not loaded, which answers keep as the response showed them.

requested_paths.description: Exact relevant file paths from the artifact inventory, relative to the application root, analyzed in first-request order before unselected scopes; no globs or implicit dependencies. Omit to analyze all sources.

__schema534.description: Signature type-name resolution was examined, including unresolved operands; v2 also renders readable operand names, v1 retains raw operand text; null means no attestation, including historical or capacity-limited Evidence.

__schema536.description: Whether all NestedClass rows were read and valid. Null for historical Evidence; false means current nesting is incomplete. Individual name digests can remain unresolved for missing, cyclic or over-deep enclosing chains.

__schema542.description: Examined zero-based MethodDef row interval before declaring-type selection; null means the row scope was not recorded. Row coordinates are build-local and cannot prove cross-build member absence for a page.

coverage.description: Coverage of ELF symbols, independent data headers, AOT kind, extents and agreeing hashes
Coverage of the bounded printable-run projection; independent of snapshot header validity

end.description: Inclusive last address of this observed body range.

__schema696.description: Observed rows; null when facet_availability declares the facet unavailable, so no rows is not evidence of none.

__schema698.description: Observed rows; null when the dossier did not record the facet (the native facet view reports it not recorded), so no rows is not evidence of none.

__schema700.description: Observed rows; null when value_flow.available is false because native_value_flow was not recorded or the provider declared it unavailable (unknowns names which), so no rows is not evidence of none.

encoding_status.description: Whether the provider declares the encoding or REA infers it from the typed bytes and native display. This does not establish the original source's intended encoding.

__schema730.description: Procedure search only: the procedure's secondary names that matched. value stays its primary name.

__schema733.description: Original provider display text, which may shorten the typed object.

__schema735.description: When present, value retains native display text because typed bytes could not be decoded.

__schema803.description: RFC 6901 pointer in the producer's reported object.

scope.description: An omitted property name; pointer identifies its actual parent, not an invented child coordinate.

__schema823.description: Exact recorded step indices; omitted selects all, [] selects none.

__schema826.description: Exact recorded transaction IDs; omitted selects all, [] selects none.

observed_at.description: Wall-clock time the provider observed the request start; absent in captures made before it was recorded.

__schema861.description: Wall-clock time the browser started the request, as it reported at completion; absent when it reported none.

__schema862.description: Milliseconds from the request start to the end of its response, as the browser timed it; absent when it reported none.

__schema893.description: Original DNS wire label bytes in order, as lowercase hex strings; the root terminator is excluded. Null or omission means unknown wire identity; display text alone does not establish identity.

__schema928.description: Symbol-table `name` without the one leading underscore Darwin adds to language-level symbols (`_main` is `main`, `__ZN3rea3addEii` is `_ZN3rea3addEii`), as LLDB and dlsym name it and observe_native_calls function breakpoints accept; a name without that underscore, such as `-[Class selector]`, is unchanged. Null when `name` is null, nothing remains, or the Evidence predates this field.

cryptid.description: Encryption system identifier as recorded; loader.h defines 0 as not encrypted.

cryptoff.description: File offset of the range from the start of the slice; null when cmdsize is too short to hold it.

pad.description: LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO_64 padding word; null for the 32-bit form.

__schema951.description: Exact name, called-method target_name or accessed field_name; empty matches nothing.

__schema955.description: Exact defining type (fields/methods), parent type (member_refs), or target type (call_edges/field_accesses). Filters intersect.

resolved_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the raw signature with each TypeDef or TypeRef operand replaced by that type's namespace-qualified name; equals raw_sha256 when the signature names no types. Unlike raw_sha256 it does not depend on build-local metadata rows. Null when the signature could not be decoded or names a type REA could not resolve, such as a TypeSpec.

value.description: Encoded scalar, not runtime state. i8/u8 are decimal strings; negative zero and nonfinite floats are -0/NaN/Infinity/-Infinity strings. Null is a decoded class null only when state is decoded.

__schema978.description: Match any exact retained intent action; no substring matching

__schema980.description: Exact resolved class names or declared component names; no substring or alias guessing

__schema982.description: Exact exported declaration; null selects omitted or unresolved declarations. exported_default is separate.
